Big Horn Recreation Site.accessType: Launch (open gravel/sand clearing to the water)
Big Horn Recreation Site.operator: Bureau of Land Management (Wenatchee Field Office)
Big Horn Recreation Site.sourceName: Access: BLM Yakima River Canyon page (lists Bighorn among BLM's five developed river access sites). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking, checked on Esri World Imagery
Big Horn Recreation Site.note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate placed from satellite imagery and confirmed by North's own circled marking and Google Maps coordinate (46.8939898, -120.5004652), checked on Esri World Imagery z19 (z20 not available), 2026-10-25. Agency published no exact launch coordinate: BLM's National Recreation Site Points layer has no Bighorn feature. On imagery (research/raw/batch4/bhN.png, bhN_w.png, bh19c_g.png) the point sits inside an open gravel/sand clearing that runs from a small paved pull-off and structure beside SR 821 down to the Yakima's north-east shore. The clearing's water-side tip is about 8.5 m SSW (~46.89392, -120.50051). The point is not in the water, not on the road and not in the paved lot (the lot edge is ~15 m NE). Offsets: 426 m SE of the earlier v1/AW candidate (46.8965, -120.5047, an opening near the campground's NW end, now superseded); ~130 m SE of the Google 'Bighorn Boat Ramp' label pin. Our georeference of North's screenshot (Esri features + scale bar) gave a water end within ~9 m of this point. Legal access: BLM's Yakima River Canyon page (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds) lists it among BLM's five developed river access sites (Bighorn, Umtanum, Lmuma Creek, Big Pines, Roza), open year-round; fees $5 day-use, $15 overnight. Spot-check first: no ramp surface is visible (natural launch), and the imagery date is unknown.
Big Horn Recreation Site.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
Big Horn Recreation Site.bankNote: Facing downstream (NHDPlus HR flow bearing ~128, SE through the canyon), the launch is on the north-east bank, left of the NHD centreline (~41 m; ftype 558 artificial path). On imagery SR 821 runs along the same (left) bank and the railway along the opposite (right, south-west) bank.

Imagery shows a ramp to the shore south of the lot near 46.4838, -122.7311, and boatlaunchmap/OSM give 46.48381, -122.73049, but neither is an agency source, and OSM maps a second unnamed ramp about 400 m upstream. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch3/lakewen.png) puts it at the water end of a ramp/dock on the south shore of the narrow lake outlet, where the Wenatchee River leaves the lake. Legal access: State Parks' Lake Wenatchee page (https://parks.wa.gov/find-parks/state-parks/lake-wenatchee-state-park) lists the watercraft launch; Discover Pass required ($45/yr, $10/day) plus a $7/day Watercraft Launch Fee; hours summer 6:30 a.m.-dusk, winter 8 a.m.-dusk. Caveat: this is a lake-side launch at the outlet, so boaters paddle a short distance into the river.

White Bluffs Boat Launch.operator: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Hanford Reach National Monument)
White Bluffs Boat Launch.sourceName: USFWS Facilities/Property points (public view), 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp' (ObjectID 1215, asset 10004685, Public_Use 'Public Use', status Valid)
White Bluffs Boat Launch.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is USFWS's own asset point for the ramp, separate from its 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp Parking' point (46.675380, -119.453112). Legal access: USFWS Hanford Reach pages (https://www.fws.gov/national-monument/hanford-reach and .../visit-us/activities/boating---motorized) describe the concrete two-lane White Bluffs Boat Launch on the Wahluke Unit. It is CLOSED to launching motorized craft Nov 1-Jun 30 (waterfowl sanctuary), but loading/unloading non-motorized craft (canoes, kayaks, rafts) is allowed year-round, though you may have to carry boats to/from the parking lot. Monument is open sunrise to sunset; the launch is open 2 h before sunrise to 2 h after sunset for fishing entry (USFWS 2025 regulations brochure).
